musa-pedestris-three-centuries-of-cantin:
John S. Farmer collected and annotated three centuries of canting songs and slang rhymes. The dates run from 1536 to 1896. Cant was the secret slang of beggars, thieves, and street folk. Farmer prints their ballads with notes and indexes of titles and authors.

Songs here come from Dekker, Middleton, Pierce Egan, and many unnamed singers. Titles promise beggars' curses, cadgers' balls, and costers' serenades. Some are coarse, some comic, and all are rich in lost street speech. The book saves the songs of the poor and the rogue. Scholars of slang and song still mine it for early low-life verse.
the-lives-of-the-twelve-caesars-volume-1: This volume collects Suetonius's surviving sketches of Rome's teachers — the grammarians and rhetoricians who educated the empire's elite. These short lives preserve precious details about how Romans learned to read, write, and argue. Though fragmentary, the book is a goldmine for anyone curious about schooling and scholarship in the ancient world.
